Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details the financial mechanics and media buying economics of IM8's growth strategy, breaking down their public P&L, CAC evolution, cohort payback periods, and the impact of a $1B marketing financing facility on their aggressive acquisition scaling. modules: [ADC] topics: [attribution and modeling, scaling, campaign setup and tracking] tier: 2 scope_hint: core

Topics. attribution and modeling / Deconstructing IM8's financial reporting and unit economics, specifically challenging their stated 3:1 LTV-to-CAC ratio. Analyzing cohort behavior to reveal a declining 6-month Gross Profit (GP) to CAC ratio (dropping from 2x to 1.03x over six quarters). Identifying the risks of projecting 36-month LTV multipliers when the oldest cohort is only 20 months old, and contextualizing the impact of scaling volume on cohort degradation. scaling / Executing aggressive acquisition scaling by tolerating extended CAC payback periods (6 to 8 months), subsidized by a unique $1B non-dilutive financing facility that covers 70% of upfront cohort marketing costs. Driving Average Order Value (AOV) upwards—from $142 to $212—by shifting default checkout funnels from monthly to quarterly subscription plans, enabling the brand to absorb a rising CAC (from $14 to $300+) while maintaining cohort profitability. campaign setup and tracking / Mapping post-click traffic flows to optimize conversion rates across the funnel. Routing top-of-funnel traffic (unaware/problem-aware) to third-party advertorials or quiz funnels to educate before converting. Routing solution-aware traffic directly to highly congruent, persona-specific landing pages (e.g., matching a GLP-1 ad to a GLP-1 landing page), while directing bottom-of-funnel retargeting traffic straight to core product display pages (PDPs).

Look for. The definition of IM8's projected LTV-to-CAC ratio: a 3:1 ratio based on a 36-month payback period. The primary mechanism IM8 used to increase Average Order Value (AOV) to absorb a rising CAC: shifting default checkouts from monthly to quarterly subscription plans. The details of the $1B financing facility: a non-dilutive loan that self-liquidates 70% of upfront marketing costs per cohort, repaid based on that cohort's subsequent income. The trend in the 6-month Gross Profit (GP) to CAC ratio: a steady decline from 2x down to 1.03x over the last six quarters as volume scaled.

Skip. Detailed breakdowns of ad creative scripts (e.g., the "clock/timeline" mechanism), evaluations of the specific visual elements on the landing pages, or the celebrity ambassador equity model (e.g., David Beckham).
